family.description: This domain is found in uncharacterised bacterial proteins, including the putative peptidoglycan hydrolase Rv2525c from Mycobacterium tuberculosis [[cite:PUB00100887],[cite:PUB00100886]]. It has been proposed to function as a peptidoglycan hydrolase with glycosidase activity regarding structural studies showed that this domain has a typical TIM-barrel-like fold, characteristic of glycoside hydrolases [[cite:PUB00100887]]. However, it displays esterase activity toward p-nitrophenyl esters of various acyl chain length in vitro [[cite:PUB00100886]].
family.name: Rv2525c-like, glycoside hydrolase-like domain
